summary: Built the environment module from scratch (all under /home/user/SimBuild/src/modules/environment/: index.js, atmosphere.js, sky.js, shaders.js, lighting.js, rain.js, noise.js, showcase.js; ~1390 lines). Sky: physically based single-scattering atmosphere (Rayleigh + Mie + ozone, quadratic sample spacing, faked multiple scattering) rendered into a 512x256 half-float equirect LUT only when the sun moves >0.6 deg or weather changes; the LUT feeds PMREM (scene.environment, throttled to every 2.5 s) and a full-resolution dome that adds a sun disc with hue-preserving brightness and aureole, a moon with correct phase (lit by the real sun direction) and noise maria plus halo, a hashed two-layer twinkling starfield and a faint milky-way band, and two wind-driven cloud layers (cumulus on a curved 1500 m shell with self-shadowing toward the light, silver-lining forward scatter, distance haze; stretched cirrus at 6500 m). Light: three/examples/jsm/csm/CSM.js with 3 cascades x 2048 (from QUALITY), fade on, hardware PCF (PCFShadowMap set explicitly so the r185 deprecation warning is gone), maxFar adapting to camera distance; the cascades switch from sun to moon at night. Sun/moon colour and intensity come from a JS port of the transmittance integral every frame (golden hour orange, noon neutral, blue-hour dim, moon 0.03x blue-tinted), exposure curve 1.25 day -> 3.0 night via renderer.toneMappingExposure, scene.environmentIntensity 0.8. Global ShaderChunk overrides (installed after CSM's own): height fog with exp falloff whose colour is sampled per pixel from the sky LUT in the view direction (so terrain dissolves exactly into the sky; fog is tone-mapped in-shader to match) plus sun in-scatter, and cloud shadows multiplied into the CSM directional term from a 256^2 cloud-thickness map (rendered from the same noise as the dome, 6 km world square, one tap). Every lit material in the scene is hooked automatically each frame (chained onBeforeCompile with a stable customProgramCacheKey; lit ShaderMaterials get the CSM defines/uniforms so they do not receive 3x sun); api.setupMaterial for explicit use. Weather: presets clear/partly/cloudy/rain/fog (?weather= respected), world.weather.cloudiness/rain/wind/fogDensity/wetness dynamics, GPU-animated instanced rain streaks (1 draw), fog preset attenuates direct sun; publishes sunDir, sunIntensity, skyLight every frame plus moonDir, lightDir, lightIntensity, sunColor, exposure, night, preset, and emits weather:changed. api: setWeather(preset|partial), getWeather, getSunDirection, getMoonDirection, getLightDirection, getExposure, getNight, setupMaterial, refreshEnvironment, presets, _debug. Showcase: 8 km PBR ground with Poly Haven aerial_grass_rock (anti-tiling dual-scale blend, noise-driven lush/dry macro patches, wetness darkening/roughness), an InstancedMesh of 9 spheres with per-instance roughness/metalness attributes (dielectric ladder, chrome, copper, coloured), and one InstancedMesh of 30 concrete_wall_008 blocks/towers with per-instance UV scaling, window grid with reveals and per-window random warm/cool lights at night; extra camera presets sunset/sunrise/moonrise/sky. Manifest: appended CC0 Poly Haven concrete_wall_008 (aerial_grass_rock had been added concurrently by another builder) and ran tools/fetch-assets.mjs. Verified by ~40 screenshots plus the final gauntlet /home/user/SimBuild/shots/environment/rdev1/summary.json: 16/16 shots OK, maxDrawCalls 10 (budget 15; 11 with rain), maxTriangles 111554, errors 0, only warning is core's RGBELoader deprecation. SwiftShader fps is honestly poor: the tool reports 0 (its 1.5 s window sees 1 frame) or 13.1 when the GPU queue is still absorbing frames; my own steady-state probes give 0.5-1 fps, which profiling attributes to per-pixel texture-tap volume of a full-screen PBR ground with CSM+IBL+normal maps at 1080p (anisotropy, tangents and ARM-tap removal made no difference); JS side is 0.2-1.1 ms/frame. Real-GPU fps unmeasured. Core notes written to /h
